summary: A tam ox gored several oxen one after another. Rabbi Meir says the last one hurt gets paid first. Rabbi Shimon explains how the value of the ox is shared among everyone.

chunks.en: An ox that gored four or five
chunks.st: With regard to an innocuous ox that gored four or five other

chunks.en: oxen one after the other,
chunks.st: oxen one after the other,

chunks.en: he pays the last one of them first.
chunks.st: its owner shall pay the owner of the last one of them half of the damages from the proceeds of the sale of the belligerent ox;

chunks.en: And if there is extra money left in it,
chunks.st: and if there is surplus value left in his ox after he pays that owner,

chunks.en: he gives it to the one before him.
chunks.st: he shall return it to the owner of the previous ox that was gored;

chunks.en: And if there is still extra in it,
chunks.st: and if there is still surplus value left in his ox after he pays that owner,

chunks.en: he gives it to the one before that.
chunks.st: he shall return it to the one prior to the previous one.

chunks.en: And the very last one gains,
chunks.st: The principle is that the owner of the latest of the oxen gored in succession gains.

chunks.en: say the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says that the division of the compensation is as follows:

chunks.en: An ox worth two hundred that gored
chunks.st: With regard to an innocuous ox worth two hundred dinars that gored

chunks.en: an ox worth two hundred,
chunks.st: an ox worth two hundred dinars, thereby killing it,

chunks.en: and the dead body is worth nothing,
chunks.st: and the carcass is worthless,

chunks.he: זֶה נוֹטֵל מָנֶה וְזֶה נוֹטֵל מָנֶה.
chunks.en: this one takes a maneh and that one takes a maneh.
chunks.explain: A maneh is one hundred zuz, half the ox's worth.
chunks.st: the injured party takes one hundred dinars, i.e., half the cost of the damage, from the proceeds of the sale of the belligerent ox, and the owner of the belligerent ox takes the remaining one hundred dinars.

chunks.he: חָזַר וְנָגַח שׁוֹר אַחֵר שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם,
chunks.en: If it then gored another ox worth two hundred,
chunks.st: If the ox, after goring the first ox but before compensation had been paid, again gored another ox worth two hundred dinars, and the carcass is worthless,

chunks.en: the last one takes a maneh,
chunks.st: the owner of the last ox that was gored takes one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and for the one before: this one takes fifty zuz
chunks.st: and with regard to payment for the previous goring, the owner of this ox that was gored takes fifty dinars, which is half the remaining value of the belligerent ox after one hundred dinars were paid to the last injured party,

chunks.en: and that one takes fifty zuz.
chunks.st: and the owner of that belligerent ox takes the remaining fifty dinars.

chunks.he: חָזַר וְנָגַח שׁוֹר אַחֵר שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם,
chunks.en: If it then gored another ox worth two hundred,
chunks.st: If the ox, after goring the first two oxen but before compensation had been paid, again gored another ox worth two hundred dinars, and the carcass is worthless,

chunks.en: the last one takes a maneh,
chunks.st: the last injured party takes one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: the one before him, fifty zuz,
chunks.st: the previous one takes fifty dinars,

chunks.en: and the first two
chunks.st: and the first two, i.e., the first injured party and the owner of the belligerent ox, divide the remainder, each receiving

chunks.en: get a gold dinar each.
chunks.explain: A gold dinar is worth twenty-five zuz.
chunks.st: one gold dinar, which is worth twenty-five silver dinars.

summary: An ox can be mu'ad for some things and not for others: some animals, some people, or even only on Shabbos. The owner pays in full for what it is mu'ad for, and half for the rest.

chunks.en: An ox that is mu'ad for its own kind
chunks.st: With regard to an ox that is forewarned with regard to its own species, as it already gored other oxen three times,

chunks.en: but not for other kinds,
chunks.st: but is not forewarned with regard to other species;

chunks.en: mu'ad for people but not for animals,
chunks.st: or an ox that is forewarned with regard to people, but is not forewarned with regard to animals;

chunks.en: mu'ad for small ones but not for big ones:
chunks.st: or one that is forewarned with regard to small specimens of a species, but is not forewarned with regard to large specimens of that species;

chunks.en: for what it is mu'ad for,
chunks.st: in all these cases, if the ox gores the type of animal or person with regard to which it is forewarned,

chunks.en: he pays full damage,
chunks.st: its owner pays the full cost of the damage,

chunks.en: and for what it is not mu'ad for,
chunks.st: and if it gores an animal or person with regard to which it is not forewarned,

chunks.en: he pays half damage.
chunks.st: he pays half the cost of the damage.

chunks.en: They said in front of Rabbi Yehuda:
chunks.st: The Sages said before Rabbi Yehuda:

chunks.en: What if it was mu'ad for Shabbos
chunks.st: What would be the halakha if this ox is forewarned with regard to Shabbatot

chunks.en: but not for weekdays?
chunks.st: but is not forewarned with regard to weekdays?

chunks.en: He said to them:
chunks.st: He said to them:

chunks.en: For Shabbos he pays full damage,
chunks.st: For damage it causes on Shabbatot its owner pays the full cost of the damage,

chunks.en: and for weekdays he pays half damage.
chunks.st: and for damage it causes on weekdays, he pays half the cost of the damage.

chunks.en: When is it tam again?
chunks.st: When is it rendered innocuous again after being forewarned with regard to Shabbat?

chunks.en: When it stops goring for three Shabbosos.
chunks.st: It reverts to its innocuous status when its behavior reverts to normal, i.e., when it refrains from goring for three days of Shabbat, i.e., Shabbat in three successive weeks.

summary: When an ox of a regular Jew and an ox of hekdesh gore each other, no one pays. The mishnah also teaches about an ox of a non-Jew.

chunks.en: An ox of a Jew that gored
chunks.st: With regard to an ox of a Jew that gored a

chunks.en: an ox of hekdesh,
chunks.explain: Hekdesh means it belongs to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: consecrated ox, and

words.note: Something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: וְשֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנָּגַח לְשׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: or an ox of hekdesh that gored an ox of a Jew:
chunks.st: conversely, a consecrated ox that gored a non-sacred ox, i.e., an ox owned by a Jew,

chunks.en: he does not pay, as it says, "the ox of his friend,"
chunks.st: the owner of the ox is exempt from paying compensation, as it is stated: “And if one man’s ox hurts the ox of another” (Exodus 21:35).

chunks.en: and not an ox of hekdesh.
chunks.st: It is derived from the phrase “the ox of another” that one is liable only if it is a non-sacred ox, but not if it is a consecrated ox, which belongs to the Temple treasury, regardless of whether the latter was the ox that gored or the ox that was gored.

chunks.en: An ox of a Jew that gored
chunks.st: With regard to an ox of a Jew that gored

chunks.en: an ox of a non-Jew,
chunks.st: the ox of a gentile,

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. וְשֶׁל נָכְרִי שֶׁנָּגַח לְשׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: he does not pay. And an ox of a non-Jew that gored an ox of a Jew,
chunks.st: the owner of the belligerent ox is exempt from liability. But with regard to an ox of a gentile that gored the ox of a Jew,

chunks.en: whether tam or mu'ad,
chunks.st: regardless of whether the goring ox was innocuous or forewarned,

chunks.en: he pays full damage.
chunks.st: the owner of the ox pays the full cost of the damage.

summary: Rules for an ox belonging to someone who is deaf, not of sound mind, or a child. Also, an ox trained to fight in a stadium is not put to death.

chunks.en: An ox of a person with full understanding that gored
chunks.st: If an ox of a halakhically competent person gored

chunks.en: an ox of a deaf person,
chunks.st: an ox of a deaf-mute,

words.note: Someone who cannot hear or speak.

chunks.en: a person not of sound mind, or a child,
chunks.st: an imbecile, or a minor, all of whom are not considered halakhically competent,

words.en: a person not of sound mind

chunks.en: he must pay. But an ox of a deaf person,
chunks.st: the owner is liable for damages. But if an ox of a deaf-mute,

chunks.en: a person not of sound mind, or a child,
chunks.st: an imbecile, or a minor gored

words.en: a person not of sound mind

chunks.en: that gored an ox of a person with full understanding,
chunks.st: an ox of a halakhically competent person,

chunks.en: does not pay. If an ox of a deaf person,
chunks.st: the owner of the ox is exempt from liability. If an ox belonging to a deaf-mute,

chunks.en: a person not of sound mind, or a child gored,
chunks.st: an imbecile, or a minor gored another ox and caused damage,

words.en: a person not of sound mind

chunks.en: beis din sets up a guardian for them,
chunks.st: the court appoints a steward for them

words.note: Someone who takes care of things for them.

chunks.en: and they warn in front of the guardian.
chunks.explain: Then the ox can become mu'ad.
chunks.st: and warns them with regard to the ox that gored in the presence of the steward.
chunks.stMore: The ox is thereby rendered a forewarned ox, since the steward is considered its owner with regard to the requirement of the verse: “And warning has been given to its owner” (Exodus 21:29). If, after the ox was rendered forewarned in this manner,

chunks.en: If the deaf person could now hear,
chunks.st: the deaf-mute regained his hearing,

chunks.en: the person became of sound mind, or the child grew up,
chunks.st: the imbecile became halakhically competent, or the minor reached the age of majority,

words.en: the one not of sound mind

chunks.en: it goes back to being tam.
chunks.st: the ox has thereby reverted to its status of innocuousness.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir,
chunks.stMore: who maintains that the ox had the status of a forewarned ox only while it was under the custody of the steward.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: It stays as it was.
chunks.st: It retains its previous status of being forewarned.

chunks.en: A stadium ox is not put to death,
chunks.explain: A stadium ox was trained to fight.
chunks.st: If a stadium [ha’itztadin] ox, i.e., one that is trained to fight in a stadium, gores and kills a person, it is not liable to be put to death,

chunks.en: as it says, "If an ox gores,"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And if an ox gores a man or a woman” (Exodus 21:28).

chunks.en: and not if people made it gore.
chunks.st: This is referring only to an ox that gores on its own initiative, but not to the case of an ox where others induced it to gore.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, the owner of a stadium ox, which is trained to gore, is exempt from liability if it does.

summary: If an ox kills a person, it is put to death, and if it was mu'ad the owner pays kofer. If it kills a servant, the owner pays thirty sela'im.

chunks.en: An ox that gored a person, and he died:
chunks.st: With regard to an ox that gored a person and the person died,

chunks.en: if mu'ad, he pays kofer,
chunks.explain: Kofer is money paid to the family to make up.
chunks.st: if the ox was forewarned its owner pays ransom,

words.note: Ransom money paid to the family.

chunks.en: and if tam, he does not pay kofer.
chunks.st: but if it was innocuous he is exempt from paying the ransom.

chunks.en: And both of them are put to death.
chunks.st: And both this forewarned ox and that innocuous ox are liable to be put to death for killing a person.

chunks.en: And the same for a boy and the same for a girl.
chunks.st: And the same halakha applies in a case where the animal killed a boy and the same applies in a case where it killed a girl.

chunks.en: If it gored a servant or a maidservant,
chunks.st: If the ox gored and killed a Canaanite slave or a Canaanite maidservant,

chunks.en: he gives thirty sela'im,
chunks.st: its owner gives the victim’s master thirty sela,

chunks.en: whether he is worth a maneh, or
chunks.st: whether he was a slave worth one hundred maneh, i.e., one hundred silver dinars,

chunks.en: he is worth only one dinar.
chunks.st: or worth only one dinar.

summary: An ox that kills a person by accident, while trying to do something else, is not put to death.

chunks.en: An ox that was rubbing against a wall,
chunks.st: If an ox was rubbing against a wall, and as a result the wall

chunks.en: and the wall fell on a person;
chunks.st: fell on a person and killed him;

chunks.en: or it meant to kill an animal
chunks.st: or if the ox intended to kill another animal

chunks.en: and killed a person;
chunks.st: but killed a person;

chunks.en: or meant to kill a non-Jew and killed a Jew;
chunks.st: or if it intended to kill a gentile but killed a Jew;

chunks.en: or meant to kill a baby that could not live, and killed one who could: it is not put to death.
chunks.st: or intended to kill a non-viable baby but killed a viable person; in all these cases the ox is exempt from being killed.

summary: Even an ox that belongs to a woman, to orphans, or to hekdesh is put to death if it kills a person. Rabbi Yehuda says an ox with no owner is not.

chunks.en: An ox of a woman,
chunks.st: With regard to an ox belonging to a woman, and similarly an ox belonging to orphans,

chunks.en: an ox of orphans,
chunks.st: and an ox belonging to orphans that is in the custody

chunks.en: an ox of a guardian,
chunks.st: of their steward,

chunks.en: an ox of the desert,
chunks.st: and a desert ox, which is ownerless,

chunks.en: an ox of hekdesh,
chunks.st: and an ox that was consecrated to the Temple treasury,

chunks.he: שׁוֹר הַגֵּר שֶׁמֵּת וְאֵין לוֹ יוֹרְשִׁים,
chunks.en: an ox of a ger who died and has no one to inherit him,
chunks.st: and an ox belonging to a convert who died and has no heirs, rendering the ox ownerless;

chunks.en: all these are put to death.
chunks.st: all of these oxen are liable to be put to death for killing a person.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: An ox of the desert,
chunks.st: A desert ox,

chunks.en: an ox of hekdesh,
chunks.st: a consecrated ox,

chunks.en: an ox of a ger who died,
chunks.st: and an ox belonging to a convert who died are

chunks.en: are not put to death,
chunks.st: exempt from being put to death,

chunks.en: because they have no owners.
chunks.st: since they have no owners.

summary: If an ox is about to be stoned and its owner gives it to hekdesh, it does not count. If he does it before the beis din decides, it counts.

chunks.he: שׁוֹר שֶׁהוּא יוֹצֵא לְהִסָּקֵל וְהִקְדִּישׁוֹ בְעָלָיו,
chunks.en: An ox going out to be stoned, whose owner made it hekdesh,
chunks.st: With regard to an ox that is leaving court to be stoned for killing a person and its owner then consecrated it,

chunks.en: is not hekdesh.
chunks.st: it is not considered consecrated,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the consecration does not take effect, since deriving benefit from the ox is prohibited and the ox is therefore worthless.

chunks.en: If he shechted it, its meat is forbidden.
chunks.st: If one slaughtered it, its flesh is forbidden to be eaten and it is prohibited to derive benefit from it.

chunks.en: But if before
chunks.st: But if its owner consecrated it before

chunks.en: the judgment was over, its owner made it hekdesh,
chunks.st: its verdict

chunks.en: it is hekdesh. And if he shechted it,
chunks.st: the ox is considered consecrated, and if he slaughtered it

chunks.en: its meat is allowed.
chunks.st: its flesh is permitted.

summary: If an ox is given to someone else to watch, that person is now responsible like the owner. If the owner tied it up well and it still got out, Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Eliezer disagree whether he pays.

chunks.en: He gave it to a watchman who is not paid,
chunks.st: If the owner of an ox conveyed it to an unpaid bailee,

chunks.en: to a borrower, to a paid watchman,
chunks.st: or to a borrower, or to a paid bailee,

chunks.en: or to a renter: they take the owner's place.
chunks.st: or to a renter, and it caused damage while in their custody, they enter into the responsibilities and liabilities in place of the owner.

chunks.en: If mu'ad, he pays full damage,
chunks.st: Therefore, if it was forewarned the bailee pays the full cost of the damage,

chunks.en: and if tam, he pays half damage.
chunks.st: and if it was innocuous he pays half the cost of the damage.

chunks.en: If its owner tied it with reins
chunks.st: If the ox’s owner tied it with reins to a fence

chunks.en: and locked the gate in front of it properly,
chunks.st: or locked the gate before it in an appropriate manner,

chunks.en: and it got out and did damage,
chunks.st: but nevertheless the ox emerged and caused damage,

chunks.en: whether tam or mu'ad, he must pay.
chunks.st: whether the ox is innocuous or forewarned the owner is liable,
chunks.stMore: since this is not considered sufficient precaution to prevent damage;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says

chunks.en: a tam must pay, but a mu'ad does not,
chunks.st: that if the ox is innocuous the owner is liable even if he safeguarded it appropriately,
chunks.stMore: since the Torah does not limit the required safeguarding for an innocuous ox. But if the ox is forewarned, the owner is exempt from paying compensation for damage,

chunks.en: as it says, "And its owner did not guard it,"
chunks.st: as it is stated in the verse describing damage by a forewarned ox: “And the owner has not secured it” (Exodus 21:36),

chunks.en: and this one was guarded.
chunks.st: and this ox that was tied with reins or behind a locked gate was secured.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: The only real guarding is a knife.
chunks.explain: Only shechting it makes sure it won't do damage.
chunks.st: An ox has no sufficient safeguarding at all other than slaughtering it with a knife;
chunks.stMore: there is no degree of safeguarding that exempts the ox’s owner from liability.
